The Loire is on the long leg of its cycling orbit, 630 days from the Mars flyby to the next Earth encounter, with no passengers aboard and a caretaker crew of four: Ingrid Halvorsen, commander and flight engineer, on her fourth rotation; Tomás Araya, life support and the Garden; Priya Venkataraman, systems and comms, on her first long rotation; and Wekesa Odhiambo, flight surgeon and EVA lead, whose daughter Amani lives at Elysium Station on Mars. The ship is seventeen years old and the crew know it. Earth is four to twenty-two light-minutes away, so nothing can be asked of Darwin that is needed in the next hour.

On day 212 Priya found a new four-hertz vibration in the slip-ring bearing that LEDGER had logged as within limits. Halvorsen despun the Wheel on her say-so and Wekesa took her on her first real EVA, where she found a micrometeoroid fragment lodged between the bearing housing and a shield plate. Wekesa pulled it with medical forceps; they patched the scar and spun the Wheel back up. Halvorsen weighed the fragment, wrote it in the logbook, and told Priya that next time she brings a new signature at hour one, not hour six: she has the commander's trust now, and she knows it. The Garden lost about a third of the tomato flowers to six hours of zero g, which Tomás describes as two thirds holding. He gave Priya one of his three strawberries afterwards.

Standing tensions: Halvorsen and Tomás still argue about whether the Garden is the ship. Priya is no longer the junior member in her own head, but has not stopped keeping her list of things she does not understand about the Loire. Wekesa records a message for Amani every day.

On day 288 an X-class flare sent a proton storm over the ship and the crew spent thirty-one hours in the Cellar. Priya's shelter procedure worked and her invented card game got them through the first day; Halvorsen played. During the storm the Dish's azimuth motor B degraded and then failed, so the high-gain link to Earth is down and only the slow low-gain text link is working until someone swaps the spare from Stores on an EVA along the truss. The ticket is open and Halvorsen has underlined it; it is the next job. The storm reached Mars some hours after the Loire; Elysium sheltered for twenty hours and Amani is fine, which Wekesa learned from a forty-one-word text message Priya moved to the front of the queue. He read it three times. Tomás covered half the Garden's trays before sheltering; whether the rest took a damaging dose will not show for about a week. He has seed to replant everything except the strawberries, so there are no strawberries until Earth. Everyone's dose is within limits.

In the dark of the shelter Halvorsen told Priya, unprompted, that her son Eirik wants this to be her last rotation and that she has been failing to decide for the whole long leg. She has not decided. Nobody else knows she said it.

Standing tensions: Halvorsen and Tomás still argue about whether the Garden is the ship, more gently now. Priya is trusted and knows it, and is quietly working out why she was not afraid in the Cellar. Wekesa records a message for Amani every day and is waiting for the photograph the low-gain link could not carry. The ferries from Earth are due around day 640.
